components.title: VPMS / Tyro SDK
components.description: external vet platform · Tyro API gateway

nodes.label: Get Conversation ID
nodes.description: The vet software asks for a new conversation ID to start a claim. The insurer ID is optional and is rejected with 400 if invalid.

nodes.label: Poll Conversations in COS
nodes.description: Not a REST service. It is the COS.Poll.Services.VetHub Windows service, which runs on a timer. For each configured insurer it calls VetHub GET api/claim/newconversations?claimType={0}&NumberofClaims={1} (app setting VetHubNewConversationsAddress, VetHubService.cs:27) and starts the claim saga.

nodes.label: Submit Claim
nodes.description: Maps the COS claim to the insurer's format and sends it to the right back-end. UPM+ AU, NZ and TPN go to DAPI api/Claims/Submit; Vet Partners goes to Boomi.

nodes.label: DAPI Routing logic
nodes.description: Routing: AuthorisationHandler.cs returns 400 if the InsuranceProviderId header is missing and 401 if the insurer is not in AllowedInsurers. AuthenticationHandler.cs and TokenService.cs get a DAPI token per insurer (api/Customer/Authentication) and cache it for 5 minutes; Vet Partners uses Basic auth instead. BackendAdapter.cs:42 picks the HTTP client named after the insurer ID; InsurersClientRegistration.cs:40-52 builds one client per insurer with its own base URL, retry, timeout and circuit breaker. Vet Partners alone is handled by VetPartnersBackendAdapter (IocConfig.cs:31, PostClaimsManager.cs:36).

properties.value: appsettings.prod.json: AU -> https://api.petsure.com.au/, TPN -> https://tp-api.petsure.com.au; NZ and VP CLAPI instances have their own single-insurer settings files

nodes.label: Submit Claim
nodes.description: Writes the claim into the UPM DS_* staging tables. Source: CLAPI config SubmitClaimEndPoint; the DAPI code itself is not verified.

nodes.label: UPM Data Polling (10 min)
nodes.description: Not verified (UPM repo not accessible). Looks like a UPM job, not an API; consider moving it to the UPM+ functions lane as DS Claims ingestion job.

nodes.label: Finish Submit Claim
nodes.description: Marks the hand-off to the UPM DS_Claims table as complete after the last attachment.

nodes.label: DAPI Routing logic
nodes.description: Routing: AuthorisationHandler.cs returns 400 if the InsuranceProviderId header is missing and 401 if the insurer is not in AllowedInsurers. AuthenticationHandler.cs and TokenService.cs get a DAPI token per insurer (api/Customer/Authentication) and cache it for 5 minutes; Vet Partners uses Basic auth instead. BackendAdapter.cs:42 picks the HTTP client named after the insurer ID; InsurersClientRegistration.cs:40-52 builds one client per insurer with its own base URL, retry, timeout and circuit breaker. Vet Partners alone is handled by VetPartnersBackendAdapter (IocConfig.cs:31, PostClaimsManager.cs:36).

properties.value: appsettings.prod.json: AU -> https://api.petsure.com.au/, TPN -> https://tp-api.petsure.com.au; NZ and VP CLAPI instances have their own single-insurer settings files

nodes.label: Finish Submit Claim
nodes.description: CLAPI calls it with PUT (BackendAdapter.cs:1180).

nodes.label: Lodge
nodes.description: Called by COS after Finish Submit Claim to make UPM create the claim from DS_Claims straight away. Requires the InsuranceProviderId header; Basic auth.

nodes.label: Lodge Claim
nodes.description: Lodge endpoint (from Confluence; the code reads it from GitHub variables). AU base: upmprod.internal.petsure.com.au:9248/PETSURE_UPM_API_BASIC. TPN base: tpupm.internal.petsure.com.au:9148/TRUPANION_PROD_API_BASIC.

nodes.label: UPM Routing Logic
nodes.description: Routing: at startup the app reads CONFIGURED_INSURERS and loads a DYNAMIC_LODGE_API_{AU|TPN} block for each, each with its own HTTP client (Program.cs:78-86, 189-205). DynamicAPIAdapter.ClaimLodgeAsync (:48-57) matches the header against INSURER_CODE and sends PUT + If-Match: * to that insurer's CLAIM_LODGE_ENDPOINT. DynamicApiLodgeHttpHandler.cs adds that insurer's Basic credentials from Key Vault (DYNAMIC-API-USERNAME for AU, TPN-DYNAMIC-API-USERNAME for TPN). URLs come from GitHub variables (DYNAMIC_LODGE_API_TPN_BASE_URI and others).

nodes.label: Claw Init
nodes.description: UPM calls it with Basic auth to start the straight-through process. It forwards the claim to Clawdia's CLAW-INIT-API, authenticating with managed identity (ClawAPIAdapter.cs:28-36).

nodes.label: Write Claim
nodes.description: Clawdia writes the assessed claim to UPM (Entra ID scope Claims.ReadWrite). It checks the checksum and whether the claim is assigned to CLAWDIA.

nodes.label: Call UPM AU Write
nodes.description: Not routing: always uses the single DYNAMIC_API client with the CLAWDIA credentials (DynamicAPIAdapter.cs:36,114-116, DynamicApiHttpHandler.cs:26-32), so it only reaches UPM AU.

nodes.label: Write
nodes.description: UPM claim write endpoint, AU only. Base: upmprod-capi.internal.petsure.com.au:9248.

nodes.label: GapOnly Benefit
nodes.description: UPM pushes the assessed gap benefit, which is forwarded to COS.

nodes.label: Forward to COS AUS
nodes.description: Not routing: always uses the single COS_API client, base URL LZ_AU_COS_API_BASE_URI (CosAPIAdapter.cs:26-39). It only reaches COS AUS, which also serves TPN.

nodes.label: Gap Only Benefit
nodes.description: Receives the gap benefit from UPM via Dynamic CLAPI (claim ref and claim number, status, benefit paid, logical claims). It checks the benefit against the amount paid, saves it in COS and passes it on to VetHub. Dynamic CLAPI sends exactly this payload (GapOnlyBenefitModel, CosAPIAdapter.cs:29-39). The api/GapOnly/GapOnlyBenefit route is the cut-down one for third-party insurers (Vet Partners).

nodes.label: Update Gap Benefit Amount
nodes.description: The insurer side (COS) posts the GapOnly benefit amount for a claim. Only authorised insurance providers can call it.

nodes.label: Update Benefit on Claim
nodes.description: Routing: decides where the outcome goes based on the practice's vet software (VpmsName). Tyro: sends the outcome to the Tyro webhook unless it was already sent (then returns 409); the Tyro response is saved (UpdateGapBenefit.cs:139-191). EzyVet with the request's UpdateVPMS flag true: sends it to EzyVet (PassGapOnlyToEzyVetAsync, UpdateGapBenefit.cs:246-250). All other vet software: nothing is sent; the outcome is only stored and the vet software collects it by polling VetHub.

nodes.label: Tyro adjudicateClaim webhook
nodes.description: Tyro's webhook that receives the GapOnly outcome from VetHub. VetHub calls it with an OAuth token from auth.tyrohealth.com. Config key Tyro:TyroGapOnlyOutcomeEndpoint. Called from ExternalVetPracticeManager.cs:87.

nodes.label: CLAW-INIT-API
nodes.description: KeyVault Function App. Checks the claim, reads the CLAW on/off and audit-mode switches from Key Vault, and publishes a CloudEvent that starts the matching entry workflow. Routes by claim type (CosService.CheckCLAWConfigurations, :150-215): CSP -> PetSure.CLAW.EClaimCSP; VetHub eClaim -> EClaimVH; GapOnly (PayToServiceProvider = 1) -> GapOnly; other -> EClaimOther. If CLAW is off it returns CLAWOFF without publishing.

nodes.label: Submit Attachment
nodes.description: Uploads one attachment file to a claim. An attachment ID must first be requested with GET /api/Claim/{conversationId}/Attachment/NewConversationId.

nodes.label: predict Treatment Code
nodes.description: Not called over REST. COS ClaimsAutomationIntegration publishes the Event Grid event Petsure.ClaimsAutomation.Claim to topic ps-prod-egt-claimsautoclaims, which triggers the Logic App. The result comes back via POST api-cos-prod/api/Claims/ClaimsAutomation/Completed. The Logic App's own trigger name is not verified.

nodes.label: Submit Claim
nodes.description: The vet software submits the claim as VetXML (default) or JSON. It checks required sections, GapOnly service hours, public holidays and whether the practice can do GapOnly claims. Returns 201.

nodes.label: Sophia Junior api
nodes.description: Not verified (the Claims Automation and ML repos were not accessible).

nodes.label: GP Model Endpoint
nodes.description: Managed online endpoint ps-prd-claimsauto-gp, deployment gp-prod-deployment, workspace ps-prd-ml-ws-claimsauto, in the legacy subscription 60181c42... (ClawGP/settings.toml:132-139). Called by Clawdia's GetGPModelOutput function using app setting GP_MODEL_PREDICTION_API_URL and bearer token GP-MODEL-PREDICTION-API-TOKEN. Two models sit behind the endpoint: the GP model (sleepy_king-14.pt) and a multiple-diagnosis model (musing_onion_md.pkl). The /score path is the standard Azure ML path, not confirmed in config.

nodes.label: Case Linking
nodes.description: Not found in the GP model code; it may live elsewhere or be planned. To be confirmed.

nodes.label: Submit Claim Attachment
nodes.description: COS calls it between Submit Claim and Finish Submit Claim; forwards the attachment to DAPI api/Claims/SubmitDocument.

nodes.label: Submit Document
nodes.description: Receives claim attachments forwarded by CLAPI Submit Claim Attachment.

nodes.label: File Conent in Windows File Share
nodes.description:
The folder comes from the DestinationClaimFilePath setting. At deploy time it’s read from a Key Vault secret: the secret name is in GitHub variable CLAIM_DES_PATH and the vault in CSP_KEYVAULT. The actual paths aren’t in the repo; Confluence and the infrastructure document give them as:

AU: \\PS-BCS-PRD-API1\auapidocuments
TPN: \\PS-BCS-PRD-API1\PRD_TP_UPMClaimDoc
